mainEntity.name: What is the difference between rough-in and finish plumbing in a bathroom installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rough-in plumbing involves installing all the pipes and fittings that will be hidden behind walls and floors before the drywall and flooring are installed. This includes the water supply lines, drain lines, and vent pipes, with stub-outs for future fixtures. Finish plumbing, performed after walls and floors are complete, involves connecting the actual fixtures such as toilets, sinks, showers, and faucets to these stub-outs. Understanding this two-stage process helps in planning project timelines and coordinating with other contractors for a smooth bathroom renovation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Rough-in plumbing is the hidden pipe installation within walls and floors, while finish plumbing involves connecting fixtures like sinks and toilets to these pipes.
